A probe reproduced both effects.
+8. **[P1] Named ChatGPT/Claude OAuth acceptance is not tested end to end.** The named tests stop after authorization-request validation; the named fixture test only checks constant strings. The browser flow is a single generic, internally consistent mock and never passes through the production McpFn client authorization lifecycle.
+9. **[P2] Inspector export is not executable by the shared scenario runner.** The inspector emits a nested `{ operation }` shape, while the runner expects top-level `kind`, `tool`, `uri`, or `prompt`. A probe exported a tool call and the runner returned `Unsupported scenario operation tools.call`.

+Per-requirement defect notes:
+
+### Release and package selection (`MCP2-AC-01`, `MCP2-AC-16`)
+
+`@mcpfn/client` and `@mcpfn/inspector` are runtime dependencies of other publishable packages but are absent from `release-packages.json`. `scripts/resolve-release-tag.mjs` loads only that file and rejects unlisted slugs. This is outside `gate:mcpfn-release`, so both local and CI gates pass. Live `npm view` returned E404 for both packages at `0.0.1`; therefore workspace and temporary-tarball proof must not be described as current published-package availability.
+
+### Authorization boundary (`MCP2-AC-07`, `MCP2-AC-10`)
+
+The generic provider seam authenticates but does not invoke `AuthProvider.authorize`, even though the shared auth middleware treats that method as the resource authorization boundary. Its local `options.authorize` callback is not a substitute because existing AuthProvider policy is silently discarded. The adapter also accepts requests with no bearer header if `authenticate` returns a session, sets an empty SDK token, spreads arbitrary `principal.extra` after authoritative keys, and omits the RFC bearer challenge on rejection.
+
+The hosted authorization handler is a useful authorization-request validator, but it is not the complete fixed role-3 adapter described by the issue. It unconditionally advertises `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`, and `none`/`client_secret_basic`/`client_secret_post`, yet the `token(request)` callback contract exposes no capability declaration from which those values could be derived or validated. State is optional; raw token/revoke parsing and all post-authorization lifecycle behavior remain outside McpFn.
+
+### OAuth metadata fetch (`MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-07`)
+
+Client ID Metadata Documents are allow-checked once, then fetched with default redirect behavior and no deadline. A permitted public HTTPS URL can redirect to a disallowed/private or non-HTTPS target unless a custom fetch prevents it. Both request registration bodies and metadata responses are converted with `text()` before the byte cap is enforced, so content-length omission/chunking defeats the allocation bound.
+
+### Lifecycle and diagnostics (`MCP2-AC-03`, `MCP2-AC-04`)
+
+`McpFnTargetContext` includes an optional signal, but `connectInternal` supplies no signal and `close()` does not coordinate with `connectPromise`. `configure` executes after target/protocol allocation but outside the connect cleanup block. Unexpected `protocol.onclose` changes only state and leaves stale references. Diagnostic sinks are awaited as part of core control flow, so a consumer observer can abort connect/close/auth and convert successful capability execution into apparent failure.
+
+### Reports and redaction (`MCP2-AC-04`, `MCP2-AC-13`, `MCP2-AC-15`)
+
+The key regex's unanchored `authorization` alternative treats public discovery field names as secrets. The URL query regex does not cover `api_key`, `password`, `cookie`, or generic credential names and never redacts fragments. `runScenarios` records raw exception messages. `runMcpFnTargetSuite` copies raw custom target descriptors. Inspector events and snapshots have no count or byte cap. These behaviors violate both secrecy and diagnostic usefulness.
+
+### OAuth proof (`MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-08`)
+
+The Playwright flow proves an internally consistent local mock can approve, exchange, refresh/rotate, and revoke. It does not use the named fixtures or production `McpFnClient.completeAuthorization` path. The ChatGPT/Claude tests call `/authorize` and receive application JSON; they do not generate a code or call `/token`. No test covers state replay, production callback failure cleanup, refresh serialization, token-auth method negotiation, expiry/denial in the browser lane, or named invalid metadata beyond a redirect mismatch.
+
+### Inspector/scenario contract (`MCP2-AC-15`)
+
+`McpFnInspector.exportScenario` returns `{name, operation: {kind, name, arguments}, expect}`. `runScenarios` expects `{name, kind, tool|uri|prompt, arguments, expect}`. The mismatch is structural and reproduced directly. Even after flattening, an inspector `CallToolResult` cannot be assigned wholesale to the runner's narrow tool expectation without an explicit conversion contract.
+
+### Server declaration (`MCP2-AC-02`)
+
+The declaration says it is side-effect-free but mutates a caller-supplied registry when item arrays are also provided. Its `manifest()` uses declaration-time capabilities, while `createServer(runtime)` can add `additionalCapabilities` and task-store flags. A probe produced `{}` from the declaration manifest and `{logging:{}}` from the runtime manifest for the same declaration, undermining the same-declaration release/test guarantee.

+## Recommendations (ranked)
+
+1. **Block merge/release and repair the trusted authorization seam** (`Intent 8, 22, 27, 28`; `MCP2-AC-07`, `MCP2-AC-10`). Invoke provider resource authorization or define one authoritative capability-aware decision contract, fail closed, prevent extra-field overrides, require/handle credentials deliberately, and emit the same bearer challenge as the resource-server handler. +2. **Make the hosted role-3 contract real or narrow its claims** (`Intent 16–27`; `MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-07`, `MCP2-AC-08`). Define adapter capabilities, derive metadata, centralize token/grant/auth-method validation and error mapping, require state/resource policy, and add independent ChatGPT/Claude code+PKCE+token+MCP flows plus incompatible cases.
+3. **Harden Client ID Metadata Document I/O** (`Intent 17, 27`; `MCP2-AC-05`, `MCP2-AC-07`). Disable automatic redirects or revalidate every hop, enforce HTTPS/address policy on each hop, add an abort deadline, stream with a byte counter, and cap decompressed bytes. Add redirect-to-private, slow, and chunked oversized vectors.
+4. **Fix lifecycle ownership before calling the client lifecycle-safe** (`Intent 10–11`; `MCP2-AC-03`, `MCP2-AC-04`). Add client/inspector release entries, validate release tag resolution, pack/install all seven packages including DataFn, run representative stdio/HTTP client/server behavior from tarballs, execute the production client example, and name an in-scope parity consumer or explicitly revise the criterion.

Audit complete: MCP-2 is **not merge-ready or release-ready**. Coverage is **5 PASS, 6 PARTIAL, 6 FAIL** across the 17 acceptance criteria.

Key findings:

- [release-packages.json](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/release-packages.json:57) omits the new `@mcpfn/client` and `@mcpfn/inspector` packages, so the normal release workflow cannot select them. Both return npm E404 at `0.0.1`.
- [provider-adapter.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/mcpfn/auth/src/provider-adapter.ts:43) authenticates but never calls `AuthProvider.authorize()`. A deny-all probe was accepted with zero authorization calls.
- [hosted-authorization.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/mcpfn/auth/src/hosted-authorization.ts:292) delegates raw token/revoke behavior while advertising hard-coded grants and authentication methods. The required hosted role-3 ownership is incomplete.
- Metadata-document fetching checks only the initial URL, follows redirects without revalidation or timeout, and buffers the entire body before enforcing its size limit.
- [client.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/mcpfn/client/src/client.ts:169) can become connected after `close()` completes. Configure and unexpected-close paths can also leak state.
- Diagnostic listener failures propagate into client operations. A successful state-changing tool call executed once but rejected with the observer’s error.
- [redaction.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/packages/oauth-core/src/redaction.ts:3) hides useful authorization metadata while leaking `api_key`, `password`, and fragment credentials.
- ChatGPT/Claude tests validate request shapes, not independent authorization-code + PKCE end-to-end flows.
- [inspector export](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/MCP-2/mcpfn/inspector/src/index.ts:99) produces a shape rejected by the shared scenario runner.
- The release gate does not execute the production client example—which calls nonexistent `calculator_add`—or perform a representative round trip using installed tarballs.

- All 112 focused affected-package tests passed.
- The full local Node 22 `gate:mcpfn-release` passed, matching exact-head CI.
- PR #122 remains `UNSTABLE`: the generic JavaScript failure is in UIFn, while SonarCloud separately fails its new-code reliability gate.
- Only the required audit report and append-only audit log were changed.
